faqs.question: What requirements must I meet to apply for the EB-2 NIW visa?
faqs.answer: You must meet the Matter of Dhanasar criteria: (1) Your proposed work has substantial merit and national importance; (2) You are well-positioned to advance the proposal; and (3) It would be beneficial for the U.S. to waive the job offer requirement. Additionally, you need a bachelor's degree or equivalent (master's or equivalent work experience).

faqs.question: Do I need a job offer for the EB-2 NIW?
faqs.answer: No. The National Interest Waiver (NIW) category is precisely an exemption from the job offer requirement. You must demonstrate that your work benefits the national interest of the U.S., which eliminates the need for a sponsoring employer. This gives you freedom to start a business or work wherever you wish.

faqs.question: What if I don't have a master's degree?
faqs.answer: You can qualify through a degree equivalency. If you have a bachelor's degree plus at least 5 years of progressive post-degree work experience, you can request a degree and work experience evaluation. The equivalency demonstrates that your education and experience are equivalent to a U.S. master's degree.

faqs.question: I'm a business owner — what evidence can I use for labor certification?
faqs.answer: Business owners can use: professional service invoices, client or supplier contracts, employee records, chamber of commerce certificates, licenses, advertising, media coverage, business awards, tax returns, and financial statements. If your company no longer exists, you can still use historical documentation that proves your role and contribution.

faqs.question: Who can I include in my process? (spouse, children)
faqs.answer: You can include your legally married spouse and your children under 21 years of age at the time of application. All will receive permanent residency derived from your approval. Children must remain unmarried to maintain the benefit.

faqs.question: How much does degree equivalency cost?
faqs.answer: Equivalency evaluations have variable costs depending on the provider. A complete process may cost approximately USD 400, while more basic evaluations can cost around USD 85. We guide you on the most appropriate option for your case.

faqs.question: Do documents need to be apostilled?
faqs.answer: In general, it is not a requirement to apostille academic documents for the EB-2 NIW. USCIS accepts certified translations and copies. We guide you in the correct organization of your petition according to current guidelines.

faqs.question: Can I apply if I live outside the United States?
faqs.answer: Yes, absolutely. The EB-2 NIW petition can be filed from any country. You do not need to be physically in the U.S. to start the process. Once approved, you can complete the consular process from your country of residence.

faqs.question: How long does the entire process take?
faqs.answer: With our Plan Plus, the average preparation time is 120 to 160 days. For the Unsung program, the time is 90 to 120 days. Once the petition is filed, USCIS takes between 13 and 24 months to respond, although with Premium Processing this timeframe can be reduced to 45 days.

faqs.question: What academic documents do I need?
faqs.answer: You need degrees, diplomas, certificates, and transcripts. Translations must be certified in English. We guide you on what to submit based on your country of study and how to organize the petition clearly for USCIS.

faqs.question: If I'm in a common-law relationship, do I need to get married to include my partner?
faqs.answer: Yes. To include your partner as a derivative beneficiary in the EB-2 NIW you need to be legally married. Common-law relationships are not recognized by USCIS for this purpose. If you plan to include your partner, you must enter into a legal marriage before filing the application.

faqs.question: What if I don't have academic publications?
faqs.answer: Publications are just one of the possible criteria. Awards, professional memberships, leadership in organizations, original contributions in your field, media coverage, and high salaries are also valued. We work with you to identify and strengthen your assets.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the UPP program and Plan Plus?
faqs.answer: With the Unsung program (UPP), you get the tools, templates, and coaching needed to manage your own case. If you're looking for a complete solution, our Plan Plus adds the preparation of your professional plan, testimonial writing, and full case management. It's the perfect option for those who prefer to delegate technical execution and ensure every detail.
